speaker: Ginger
intro: Good evening, Booth Camp! Ginger Snapp, ventriloquist. And this is my partner...
Chip! The cookie with the bite. Don't ask what happened to my head.
Her lips didn't move! A talking cookie, trainee. Stay focused.
She keeps missing what the audience shouts. Hecklers get away with MURDER.
Voices keep dropping out. I just smile, nod and let Chip do the talking.
Words going missing from voices. Let's investigate! Questions first.

always_clues.text: Voices drop out; she smiles and nods

options: How long has your hearing been like this?
Since school! The school hearing tests found it. It hasn't really changed since.
Found at school; the same ever since
stable
Found at school and steady since. Hold on to that clue!
What's Chip's best joke?
Why did the cookie see a doctor? It felt crummy! I'm here all week.
Chip
Does anyone in your family have hearing trouble?
My dad, and his mum, Grandma Snapp. Their hearing tests look just like mine.
Dad and his mum have the same pattern
family
A pattern down the family line. Worth knowing!
Any ear pain, drainage, dizziness, or sudden change?
None of those. Same as ever. I just need to hear the hecklers now.
No pain, drainage, dizziness or sudden change
no_red_flags
Is it both ears?
Both, about the same. Chip says my left is worse, but he's biased.
Both ears, about the same
both_ears
Can Chip sing?
Laaa-la-LAAAA! Thank you, thank you. Autographs later.
Chip

joke_line: Showbiz gold, but not a clue. Ask about her hearing!

red_flags.ask_line: Always check the red flags: pain, drainage, dizziness, sudden or fluctuating change, one ear only.
red_flags.answer: None of those. Same as ever. I just need to hear the hecklers now.
red_flags.clue: No pain, drainage, dizziness or sudden change
red_flags.card: Pain, drainage, dizziness, sudden change: NONE.

after_history: Oh! My hearing test from nine years ago. Chip never lets me lose it.
Old results are gold! No red flags so far. Let's take a look.

otoscopy.caption: Ginger's RIGHT ear: a narrow canal, shiny eardrum.
lines: Narrow canals, healthy eardrums. Nothing hiding in there.
Not even a chocolate chip? I'm insulted.

quiz.prompt: Is her middle ear the problem?
options: No sign of it: type A, both sides.
Yes: flat, type B.
Flat with a normal canal volume would point to fluid. Hers have normal peaks.
Yes: type C, negative pressure.
Her peaks sit near zero. A type C sits far to the left.

tymp.clue: Tymp: type A both ears (no fluid, no blockage)
after: Type A both sides: no fluid, no blockage. The bone test decides if it's deeper.

instructions: Tell her: press for every beep, even faint ones. Chip doesn't get a button.

audiometry.intro: Right ear's yours. Watch the middle pitches!

750: Extra stop at 750! A 500-to-1k jump of 20 dB or more gets tested in between.
Hearing aids care exactly where her loss begins. Now we know.

audiometry.intro: Left ear at Hoot speed. Same shape?
Bone check at Hoot speed: middle ear or inner ear?
before: Now the bone buzzer: middle ear, or deeper?

after_audiometry: Bone sits right on the air: no gap. Not the middle ear.

after: Words at a party? Buddy, I AM the party.

reveal.title: COOKIE BITE
ask: Here's her chart. What shape do you see?
lines: Worse in the middle, better at both ends: a cookie bite! These often run in families.
So that's why Chip and I get along.
And her right ear matches her chart from nine years ago. Stable.

evidence.prompt: What shape is Ginger's hearing loss?
options: A cookie bite: worst in the middle pitches.
A ski slope: worst in the high pitches.
A noise notch at 4k.
wrong: Look at 4k and 8k: they come back up.
Her dip is wider and at lower pitches: 1k to 2k, not 4k.
evidence.right: The middle pitches carry lots of speech, so words drop out of voices.

findings.text: Worst in the middle pitches (cookie bite)
Right ear matches nine years ago: stable

lines.fit: Sweet call! Stable for years, ears match, no red flags: hearing aids tuned for the middle pitches.
lines.refer: Family history isn't a red flag. Ears match, nothing sudden: fit her, and offer a genetics chat.
lines.today: Since SCHOOL? That's the opposite of sudden! No emergency here.

clue_pick.prompt: Her dad and grandma have it too. Why is it still safe to fit her?
clue_pick.wrong_line: True, but it doesn't show she's safe to fit. Look for the red-flag check!

wrong_lines.family: That's family history, not a red flag. What shows it's safe?
wrong_lines.ear_clear: True: no wax, drainage or deformity today. Past drips, pain, dizziness, sudden change: which clue clears those?
wrong_lines.tymp_a: True: no fluid, no blockage. Which clue clears past drips, pain, dizziness and sudden change?
wrong_lines.snhl: True: no air-bone gap, one red flag cleared. Which clue clears past drips, pain, dizziness and sudden change?
wrong_lines.voices_drop: That's what's wrong, not why it's safe. Look for the red-flag check!
wrong_lines.cookie: That's what's wrong, not why it's safe. Look for the red-flag check!

clue_pick.right_line: Exactly! History, exam and chart all clear, stable and matching: fitting is the right call.

payoff: Hearing aids tuned for the middle pitches: right where her bite is.
At the fitting we measure in her ear, then score words again with the aids on.
Oh! I can hear the back row. Even the hecklers!
It runs in families: offer a genetic counselling referral. Not a red flag, so no need to wait.
And a hearing check every year: some family patterns slowly change.
Same time next year, owl. Bring snacks.

subheads.S: A textbook cookie bite, stable for nine years, charted cleanly.
subheads.A: Stable, matching ears, no red flags: fit, tune for the middle, offer a genetics chat.
subheads.B: The bite showed up; a few stamps missed their cue.
subheads.C: Look for the dip between 1k and 2k.
subheads.Do-over: Cookie bites sit in the middle pitches. Family history alone isn't a red flag.

refer.headline: VENTRILOQUIST REFERRED FOR FAMILY HISTORY; CHIP OBJECTS

today.headline: GINGER RUSHED TO DOCTOR; CHIP ASKS 'FOR WHAT?'
today.subhead: Stable for years is the opposite of sudden.
